# UE 5.8 world technology - verified notes and recommended pipeline

Engine checked: **UE 5.8.2** (CL 56702186, `++UE5+Release-5.8`) at `W:\Unreal Engine 5\UE_5.8`.
Project: `...\UnrealSonnet55Forza` (runtime C++ module `Sonnet55Forza`, editor DLL already builds, `Content/` still empty).
Research date: 2026-10-16. All prose is my own wording; sources are listed in section 12.

Evidence tags used everywhere below:

* **[L]** verified locally: engine headers / .cpp under `Engine\Source` and `Engine\Plugins`, `.uplugin` files, engine `.ini` files, or the Python stub generated by this project's editor (`Intermediate\PythonStub\unreal.py`, 5.8-accurate, 33 MB, the authority for Python names).
* **[W]** taken from Epic documentation or other web pages (listed in section 12).
* **[I]** my inference or rule of thumb. Profile before trusting.

Related project docs that this file refines: `Docs/WORLD_SPEC.md`, `Docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (see section 11 for the deltas I recommend).

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 0. Short answer

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Landscape creation | `ALandscape::Import()` is **C++ only** (not a UFUNCTION). Wrap it in the editor module (`Sonnet55ForzaEditor`) and call the wrapper from Python. Epic's own PCG test does exactly this. |
| Landscape size | 1 m spacing is fine with Nanite. Prefer **4065 x 4065 verts, 127-quad sections x 2x2, 16x16 = 256 components** (4064 m) over the 4033 / 1024-component layout in WORLD_SPEC. 2 m spacing (2033 verts, 8x8 components) is the cheap fallback. |
| Layers | Keep the planned `layer_<Name>.r8` weightmaps (needed for per-layer physical materials). Create layer-info assets with `UE::Landscape::CreateTargetLayerInfo`. Python cannot set `layer_name` (read-only in 5.8). |
| Landscape material | Slope/height auto-blend in the material, plus script weightmaps for roadside gravel/sand/dirt. Nanite landscape ON. RVT OFF. Landscape Grass ON. |
| Roads | Landscape splines are **not scriptable** (only `GetSplineMeshComponents` is exposed). Use pre-baked chunk meshes (your Blender chunks) on a heightmap that was already carved along the road. |
| World Partition | `LevelEditorSubsystem.new_level(path, is_partitioned_world=True)`. 5.8 default runtime hash is **`WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet`** (not SpatialHash). Default range 256 m is too short for driving; tune in C++ (Python cannot reach `RuntimeHash`). |
| Streaming layout | Landscape + road chunks **always loaded** (`is_spatially_loaded=False`); stream only vegetation, props, buildings, traffic spawners. HLOD becomes optional. |
| Nanite / Lumen / VSM | Nanite on every opaque mesh incl. foliage. Software Lumen (turn off HW RT even though the project enables `r.RayTracing`), High scalability (`sg.*Quality=2`), quantize sun rotation for VSM caching. |
| Scatter | Own deterministic scatter (Foliage API `AInstancedFoliageActor::AddInstances` from Python, or a per-cell ISM actor). PCG = skip for baseline. |
| Water | Water plugin is Experimental (+ Landmass Beta). Use Ocean (+ maybe Lake) with `affects_landscape=False` and a pre-carved heightmap. Skip rivers/carving. |
| Sky / TOD | SkyAtmosphere + VolumetricCloud + ExponentialHeightFog + SkyLight (real-time capture) + 2 directional lights (sun index 0, moon index 1). Own time-of-day driver. Sea level at world Z = 0. |

## 2. Landscape

### 2.1 How to create one from a heightmap (the API reality)

[L] `ALandscapeProxy::Import(...)` in `LandscapeProxy.h` is declared `LANDSCAPE_API void Import(const FGuid&, int32 MinX, MinY, MaxX, MaxY, int32 NumSubsections, int32 SubsectionSizeQuads, const TMap<FGuid,TArray<uint16>>& HeightData, const TCHAR* HeightmapFileName, const TMap<FGuid,TArray<FLandscapeImportLayerInfo>>& LayerInfos, ELandscapeImportAlphamapType, const TArrayView<const FLandscapeLayer>&)`. It has **no UFUNCTION**, and a grep of the whole engine found no Python/Blueprint/commandlet route that creates a landscape from data. In the Python stub, `Landscape`/`LandscapeProxy` only expose `landscape_import_heightmap_from_render_target(...)` / `landscape_import_weightmap_from_render_target(...)` / `render_heightmap(...)`, which need an existing landscape. A spawned `unreal.Landscape` with no components is useless.

Two reference implementations ship with the engine and are the templates to copy:

1. `Engine\Plugins\PCG\Source\PCG\Private\Tests\PCGTestsCommon.cpp` - minimal: `SpawnActor<ALandscape>` -> `Import(FGuid::NewGuid(), 0,0,Size-1,Size-1, NumSubsections, SubsectionSizeQuads, {FGuid()->heights}, nullptr, {FGuid()->{}}, Additive, {})` -> `CreateLandscapeInfo()`.
2. `Engine\Source\Editor\LandscapeEditor\Private\LandscapeEditorDetailCustomization_NewLandscape.cpp` (`OnCreateButtonClicked`, ~line 1138-1290) - the full editor flow: spawn at `Location + Offset` (offset centres it), `SetActorRelativeScale3D` **before** Import, assign `LandscapeMaterial`, `Import`, `GetLandscapeInfo()`, `UpdateLayerInfoMap`, `AddTargetLayer(name, FLandscapeTargetLayerSettings(layerInfo))` per layer, then `ULandscapeSubsystem::ChangeGridSize(info, GridSizeInComponents)` for World Partition.

Things `Import` requires (read in `LandscapeEdit.cpp` ~3123-3330) [L]:
* `InGuid` valid; landscape actor must be blank (`LandscapeComponents.Num()==0`).
* Height data: `(MaxX-MinX+1)*(MaxY-MinY+1)` uint16, row-major with **X fastest** (`HEIGHTDATA(X,Y)=H[Y*VertsX+X]`); an empty array = flat. Keys in both TMaps must be `FGuid()` (the "final layer").
* `(Verts-1)` must be an exact multiple of `NumSubsections*SubsectionSizeQuads`, otherwise the integer division silently drops the remainder.
* Weight data: `FLandscapeImportLayerInfo{LayerName, LayerInfo, SourceFilePath, LayerData}`. `LayerData` is either empty (layer skipped) or exactly `VertsX*VertsY` bytes, row-major. A layer that has data **must have a non-null `LayerInfo`** (it dereferences `GetBlendMethod()`).
* `ELandscapeImportAlphamapType::Additive` = UE-native (weight-blended layers sum to 255 per vertex, e.g. 50/30/20%). `Layered` = each map is "remainder after the layers below", last layer 255.
* If no edit layers are passed, `Import` calls `CreateDefaultLayer()`. **Edit layers are mandatory in 5.7+** (non-layer landscapes are deprecated; `UE_DEPRECATED(5.7...)` on `HasLayersContent`).
* It opens a `FScopedSlowTask` progress dialog (fine in the editor, harmless with `-unattended`).

Valid component geometry [L] (`LandscapeConfigHelper.cpp`): `SubsectionSizeQuadsValues = {7,15,31,63,127,255}`, `NumSectionValues = {1,2}` (i.e. 1x1 or 2x2). `ULandscapeSettings::MaxComponents = 256` per axis (config). The New Landscape UI clamps total vertices to 8191 per side.

### 2.2 Sizing for roughly 4 km x 4 km

No valid component size divides 4096 (component quad counts are 7, 14, 15, 30, 31, 62, 63, 126, 127, 254, 255, 510), so the world is 4064 or 4032 m, not exactly 4096.

| Option | Spacing | Section x layout | Component quads | Components | Verts / side | World | Actor scale XY | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A (recommended)** | 1 m | 127 x 2x2 | 254 | 16 x 16 = 256 | **4065** (16.5 M verts, 33 MB r16) | 4064 m | 100 | 4x fewer components than C; 16 per axis = fits one WP landscape region (below) |
| B (cheap fallback) | 2 m | 127 x 2x2 | 254 | 8 x 8 = 64 | 2033 (4.1 M verts, 8 MB) | 4064 m | 200 | 4x faster to generate/build; road corridor must be carved a bit wider |
| C (what WORLD_SPEC says) | 1 m | 63 x 2x2 | 126 | 32 x 32 = 1024 | 4033 | 4032 m | 100 | Valid and listed in Epic's technical guide table, but equals Epic's recommended maximum (1024) and exceeds the WP region size (16) |
| D | 1 m | 255 x 2x2 | 510 | 8 x 8 = 64 | 4081 | 4080 m | 100 | Fewest components; coarse LOD granularity; only sensible with Nanite on |

Notes:
* WORLD_SPEC.md says "components of 127 quads (2x2 sub-sections of 63)". Two 63-quad sections make a **126**-quad component (127 *vertices* per side); the 4033-vertex total is right, the "127 quads" wording is not.
* Epic's guidance [W]: prefer 63 quads/section as the general default; for a large landscape use bigger sections (fewer components, less render-thread CPU); each component has a render-thread cost and each section is a draw call; stay at or below 1024 components.
* The Nanite landscape builds one Nanite mesh per up-to-8x8 components of a proxy (`NaniteComponentMaxSide = 8`, `NaniteMaxComponents = 64`) [L].
* WP editor "regions": `WorldPartitionRegionSize` default 16, range 4..64; creation with more components than that goes through the region path (`bNeedsLandscapeRegions`, needs a saved map, builds LocationVolumes) [L]. Options A, B, D (<=16 per axis) avoid it entirely.
* Rough resident cost for option A (my estimate [I]): heightmap RGBA8 ~66 MB (+mips), each 4 weight layers ~66 MB, Nanite mesh data on top, heightfield collision ~35 MB. Under 600 MB total for 6 layers, fine on a 12 GB RTX 5070.

### 2.3 Height encoding and actor transform math [L]

`LandscapeDataAccess` (`LandscapeDataAccess.h`): local height = `(uint16 - 32768) / 128`, multiplied by the actor's Z scale. At Z scale 100 that is +-256 m and 0.78 cm per step. For a custom range, pick the scale so the whole uint16 range spans your relief:

```
span_cm      = (Hmax_m - Hmin_m) * 100
ZScale       = span_cm / 512.0              # 512 = full uint16 span in local units (65535/128)
actor_Z_cm   = Hmin_m*100 + 256.0 * ZScale  # uint16 0 maps to Hmin
u16(h_m)     = clamp(round((h_m*100 - Hmin_m*100) * 128.0 / ZScale), 0, 65535)
quantum_cm   = ZScale / 128                 # e.g. 820 m span -> ZScale 160.2 -> 1.25 cm
```
This matches Epic's guide ("convert to cm, multiply by 1/512") [W]. Actor X/Y location for a landscape centred on the origin: `-(Verts-1)/2 * ScaleXY` (cm). Keep sea level at world Z = 0 (section 8). WORLD_SPEC axes (X north, Y east): `H[j,i]` with i -> +X and j -> +Y matches the engine's row-major layout, so write the r16 with row index = Y.

### 2.4 Reference C++ wrapper (editor module) - not compiled, verified API names

```csharp
// Source/Sonnet55ForzaEditor/Sonnet55ForzaEditor.Build.cs
PrivateDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new[] {
  "Core","CoreUObject","Engine","UnrealEd","AssetRegistry",
  "Landscape","LandscapeEditor",         // LandscapeEditorUtils::SetHeightmapData / SetWeightmapData
  "EditorScriptingUtilities"
});
// Sonnet55Forza.uproject: { "Name":"Sonnet55ForzaEditor","Type":"Editor","LoadingPhase":"PostEngineInit" }
// Sonnet55ForzaEditor.Target.cs: ExtraModuleNames.Add("Sonnet55ForzaEditor");   // Live Coding cannot add a module: close the editor and run UBT.
```

```cpp
#include "Landscape.h"
#include "LandscapeProxy.h"
#include "LandscapeInfo.h"
#include "LandscapeSubsystem.h"
#include "LandscapeEditTypes.h"     // UE::Landscape::EBuildFlags
#include "LandscapeUtils.h"         // UE::Landscape::CreateTargetLayerInfo
#include "LandscapeLayerInfoObject.h"
#include "LandscapeEditorUtils.h"   // module LandscapeEditor
#include "Misc/FileHelper.h"

UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category="Roam|World")
static ALandscape* CreateLandscapeFromR16(UWorld* World, const FString& R16File, int32 VertsPerSide,
    int32 QuadsPerSection, int32 SectionsPerComponent, FVector Scale /*cm/vertex, Z=ZScale*/, FVector CentreCm,
    UMaterialInterface* Material, int32 WPGridSizeInComponents, bool bAlwaysLoaded)
{
  const int32 QuadsPerComp = QuadsPerSection * SectionsPerComponent;
  if (!World || ((VertsPerSide - 1) % QuadsPerComp) != 0) return nullptr;

  TArray<uint8> Raw;
  if (!FFileHelper::LoadFileToArray(Raw, *R16File) || Raw.Num() != VertsPerSide*VertsPerSide*2) return nullptr;
  TArray<uint16> Heights; Heights.SetNumUninitialized(VertsPerSide*VertsPerSide);
  FMemory::Memcpy(Heights.GetData(), Raw.GetData(), Raw.Num());                 // little-endian == host

  const double Half = 0.5 * (VertsPerSide - 1);
  ALandscape* L = World->SpawnActor<ALandscape>(CentreCm + FVector(-Half*Scale.X, -Half*Scale.Y, 0), FRotator::ZeroRotator);
  L->SetActorRelativeScale3D(Scale);                       // BEFORE Import: normals are computed with DrawScale3D
  L->LandscapeMaterial = Material;
  L->bAreNewLandscapeActorsSpatiallyLoaded = !bAlwaysLoaded;   // proxies/spline actors created later inherit this

  TMap<FGuid, TArray<uint16>> HeightPerLayer;               HeightPerLayer.Add(FGuid(), MoveTemp(Heights));
  TMap<FGuid, TArray<FLandscapeImportLayerInfo>> LayerData; LayerData.Add(FGuid(), {});   // fill for weightmaps, see 2.5
  L->Import(FGuid::NewGuid(), 0, 0, VertsPerSide-1, VertsPerSide-1, SectionsPerComponent, QuadsPerSection,
            HeightPerLayer, TEXT(""), LayerData, ELandscapeImportAlphamapType::Additive,
            TArrayView<const FLandscapeLayer>());

  ULandscapeInfo* Info = L->GetLandscapeInfo(); if (!Info) Info = L->CreateLandscapeInfo();
  Info->UpdateLayerInfoMap(L);
  if (ULandscapeSubsystem* Sub = World->GetSubsystem<ULandscapeSubsystem>())
    if (Sub->IsGridBased()) Sub->ChangeGridSize(Info, WPGridSizeInComponents);   // converts to ALandscapeStreamingProxy actors
  L->SetActorLabel(TEXT("Landscape_Roamline"));
  return L;
}

UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category="Roam|World")
static void BuildLandscapeAll()   // grass maps + physical material + Nanite meshes
{ UE::Landscape::BuildAll(UE::Landscape::EBuildFlags::ForceRebuild | UE::Landscape::EBuildFlags::WriteFinalLog); }
```
Python side (names verified in the stub):
```python
world = unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.UnrealEditorSubsystem).get_editor_world()
ls = unreal.RoamWorldBuilder.create_landscape_from_r16(world, r"...\heightmap_4065.r16", 4065, 127, 2,
        unreal.Vector(100, 100, 160.2), unreal.Vector(0, 0, actor_z_cm), mat, 4, True)
ls.set_editor_property("enable_nanite", True)     # set via the property system so proxies inherit it (LandscapeInherited)
unreal.RoamWorldBuilder.build_landscape_all()
unreal.EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.save_dirty_packages(True, True)
```

Iterating without recreating: `LandscapeEditorUtils::SetHeightmapData(ALandscapeProxy*, const TArray<uint16>&)` and `SetWeightmapData(Landscape, LayerInfo, const TArray<uint8>&)` are exported from the LandscapeEditor module [L]. They require the array to match the landscape's full bounding rect `(W+1)*(H+1)` and write through `FHeightmapAccessor` / `TAlphamapAccessor` into the current edit layer.

### 2.5 Weightmap layers and layer-info objects

* Create the asset: `UE::Landscape::CreateTargetLayerInfo(FName LayerName, const FString& PackagePath, const FString& AssetName)` (public in `LandscapeUtils.h`). It duplicates the project default layer info if `ULandscapeSettings` has one, else `NewObject`, calls `SetLayerName`, registers with the asset registry, marks dirty. Save with `UEditorAssetLibrary::SaveLoadedAsset`.
* 5.7/5.8 change [L]: `ULandscapeLayerInfoObject` properties are now deprecated-private. Python sees `layer_name` as **Read-Only**, `phys_material`, `hardness`, `minimum_collision_relevance_weight`, `blend_method`, `blend_group` as read-write. C++ setters: `SetLayerName`, `SetPhysicalMaterial(PhysMat, bModify)`, `SetBlendMethod`, `SetHardness`.
* `bNoWeightBlend` is gone: `ELandscapeTargetLayerBlendMethod { None, FinalWeightBlending (legacy, default), PremultipliedAlphaBlending (advanced) }`. With a single edit layer (our case) legacy weight blending is fine. Use `None` for non-exclusive masks (e.g. a "wetness" or "road wear" layer).
* Import flow with layers: build one `FLandscapeImportLayerInfo` per `layer_<Name>.r8` (full `Verts*Verts` bytes, row-major), `LayerInfo` = asset above. With `Additive` the weight-blended layers should sum to 255 per vertex; normalise in `build_world.py` (put the leftover into the base "Grass" layer). Afterwards mirror the editor: `Landscape->AddTargetLayer(Name, FLandscapeTargetLayerSettings(LayerInfo))` and `Info->Layers[idx].LayerInfoObj = LayerInfo`.
* Component weight allocation: a landscape component stores layers in RGBA8 weightmap textures (4 per texture). `MaxPaintedLayersPerComponent` (Python `max_painted_layers_per_component`) limits it; 0 = unlimited. Keep <= 6-8 layers in total; every unique layer costs texture samples in the landscape material.
* Per-layer surface type (your `ERoamSurface` plan): set `phys_material` on each layer info; alternatively use the `Landscape Physical Material Output` material node (`MaterialExpressionLandscapePhysicalMaterialOutput`, present in Python) which makes the material the source of truth. The `phys_material` field is ignored if that node is used. Landscape collision stores the dominant physical layer at collision-mip resolution, rebuilt by `landscape.RebuildPhysicalMaterial` / `UE::Landscape::BuildPhysicalMaterial` (and `BuildAll`) [L]. `ALandscapeProxy::DefaultPhysMaterial` (`default_phys_material`) is the fallback.
* Holes (tunnel mouths, quarries) use the special **visibility** target layer plus `landscape_hole_material`. I did not verify a scripted import path for it. The robust alternative for tunnels is: carve a trench in the heightmap and cover it with the tunnel/rock-shell chunk mesh from Blender.

### 2.6 Landscape material: auto-blend by slope / height

Authoring from Python works: `unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary.create_material_expression(material, unreal.MaterialExpressionLandscapeLayerBlend, x, y)`, `connect_material_property`, `recompile_material` [L stub]. These expression classes exist in the stub: `MaterialExpressionLandscapeLayerBlend` (struct `LayerBlendInput` is exposed, `ELandscapeLayerBlendType {LB_WeightBlend, LB_AlphaBlend, LB_HeightBlend}`), `...LayerCoords`, `...LayerSample`, `...LayerSwitch`, `...LayerWeight`, `...VisibilityMask`, `...GrassOutput`, `...PhysicalMaterialOutput`, `MaterialExpressionRuntimeVirtualTexture*`, `MaterialExpressionVertexNormalWS`, `MaterialExpressionSmoothStep`, `MaterialExpressionWorldPosition`.

Recipe (what I would build, [I]):
1. Base ground from procedural masks, no painting needed: `slope = smoothstep(a, b, 1 - VertexNormalWS.z)` for grass->rock, `height = smoothstep(...)` on `AbsoluteWorldPosition.z` for snowline / sand-near-sea (`z` within a few metres of 0) / treeline, each perturbed by a tiled noise to avoid straight contour lines. Use `LandscapeLayerCoords` with three UV scales (macro ~40 m, mid ~8 m, micro ~1.5 m) to hide tiling.
2. Layer the painted weightmaps on top with `LandscapeLayerWeight` / `LandscapeLayerBlend` (height blend for gravel/dirt/sand) using the same layer names as the layer-info assets.
3. Blend whole material attributes (`BlendMaterialAttributes`) per surface rather than per channel to keep the graph readable; pack textures (albedo+height, normal.xy+roughness+AO) to hold samples down. Budget: <= 4 unique surface sets x 2 scales ~ 16 samples + 1 mask.
4. Add `LandscapeGrassOutput` inputs (one per grass type) fed by the same masks, so grass density follows slope/height/roadside weights without extra painting.
5. Sky Atmosphere / fog need nothing special in the material. If `Substrate` is on (it is), author Substrate-compatible slabs or let the engine convert legacy inputs.

Nanite landscape ignores per-LOD override materials (`PerLODOverrideMaterials` "not effective on Nanite landscape") [L], so one material must serve all distances.

### 2.7 Nanite landscape (ADOPT)

* Properties on `ALandscapeProxy` [L]: `bEnableNanite`, `NaniteLODIndex` (0 = full res; editor/debug), `bNaniteSkirtEnabled` + `NaniteSkirtDepth` (hide cracks between proxies), `NanitePositionPrecision`, `NaniteMaxEdgeLengthFactor` (default 16). Python names: `enable_nanite`, `nanite_lod_index`, `nanite_skirt_enabled`, `nanite_skirt_depth`, `nanite_position_precision`, `nanite_max_edge_length_factor`.
* Workflow [W]: tick Enable Nanite, then Build Data (Details) or Build > Build Landscape. Stale data triggers a warning and the editor falls back to the non-Nanite landscape; **cook rebuilds stale proxies**, which makes cooking slow, so save fully built proxies. In code: `UE::Landscape::BuildNanite(flags)` / `ULandscapeSubsystem::BuildNanite(flags, proxies)` (async per proxy; completion is tracked by `ULandscapeSubsystem::FinishAllNaniteBuildsInFlightNow`, check the log before saving).
* Memory: both the Nanite data and the classic component data stay resident (about 2x landscape data). Non-Nanite data is required for RVT and water [W].
* CVars: `landscape.RenderNanite` (default 1, runtime on/off), `landscape.Nanite.UpdateLag` (0.25 s after the last edit before a live rebuild), `landscape.Nanite.StallDetectionTimeout` (180 s), `landscape.Nanite.MultithreadBuild` and `landscape.Nanite.MaxSimultaneousMultithreadBuilds` (named in the `LandscapeSubsystem.h` comments), `landscape.NaniteExportCacheMaxQuadCount` [L]. The docs page also lists a live-rebuild-on-modification switch (default 0, experimental); keep live rebuild off while scripting [W].
* Known issue: a 5.6 bug made landscapes with more than ~64 components disappear when Nanite was on; a forum report says it is fixed in 5.7 [W, secondary]. We are on 5.8; verify with Nanite visualization after the first build.
* Nanite tessellation / displacement on the landscape material is possible but skip it (cost, no visual need at 1 m).

### 2.8 Runtime virtual texturing (SKIP)

RVT is useful for blending meshes into terrain colour and for expensive landscape materials. Reasons to skip here: with Nanite landscape the non-Nanite data must stay resident anyway [W], roads are separate meshes (no blend needed), our material is moderate, and RVT needs extra project/asset setup (`RuntimeVirtualTexture` asset + `RuntimeVirtualTextureVolume` + output/sample nodes, which do exist in the Python stub). Revisit only if the landscape material becomes the bottleneck.

### 2.9 Landscape grass (ADOPT)

`ULandscapeGrassType` -> `GrassVarieties[]` with `GrassMesh`, `GrassDensity` (per platform/quality), `StartCullDistance` / `EndCullDistance`, `PlacementJitter`, `RandomRotation`, `AlignToSurface`, `Scaling`, `bCastDynamicShadow`, `bUseGrid`; driven by `LandscapeGrassOutput` nodes in the material [L]. Runtime tuning CVars verified in `LandscapeGrass.cpp`: `grass.Enable`, `grass.CullDistanceScale`, `grass.MaxInstancesPerComponent`, `grass.MaxAsyncTasks`, `grass.MaxCreatePerFrame`, `grass.CullSubsections`, `grass.DisableGPUCull`. `ALandscape::SetGrassEnabled` is a UFUNCTION. Grass meshes must be Nanite to appear in Lumen surface cache (section 5). The 5.8 release notes say PCG's GPU runtime scatter now performs in the same range as the landscape grass system [W], so grass stays on the landscape system (no PCG needed).

### 2.10 Landscape splines vs custom road meshes

* Landscape splines (`ULandscapeSplinesComponent`, `ULandscapeSplineControlPoint`, `ULandscapeSplineSegment`, edit layer "Splines") deform the terrain, paint a layer and place spline meshes. [L] Python/Blueprint exposure is essentially nil (`GetSplineMeshComponents()` is the only UFUNCTION; creating control points/segments is C++ internals). 40-60 km of road through that API is not worth it. **SKIP.**
* `USplineMeshComponent` per segment: works with Nanite in 5.8 (Epic's Nanite page says splines are supported), but: use `FMeshNaniteSettings::MaxEdgeLengthFactor` on the mesh (Epic's own comment names Spline Mesh Component as the use case) so Nanite does not over-simplify a mesh that will be bent; known bug UE-348635 (Nanite spline mesh deforms along a different world normal than non-Nanite, targeted 5.8) [W, secondary]; 2000-3000 components cost CPU; Lumen cards degrade on deformed spline meshes [W]. Prototype only.
* **Recommended: chunked ribbon meshes on a pre-carved heightmap.** Your design (roads from `roads.json` -> Blender chunks) already matches. Engineering rules:
  1. Carve the corridor into the heightmap in `build_world.py` (grade-limited profile, crossfall, smooth shoulders, cut/fill). The road is then a mesh sitting 2-4 cm above ground that already matches it.
  2. Give the road mesh **thickness** (skirt 30-50 cm down). Lumen software tracing uses distance fields; Epic says thin walls under about 10 cm leak light [W].
  3. Nanite on, material opaque (Nanite supports Opaque and Masked only [W]). Collision "Use Complex Collision As Simple" or dedicated simple shapes; check with `show collision`. In Python: `unreal.GeometryScript_NewAssetUtils.create_new_static_mesh_asset_from_mesh(...)` options expose `enable_nanite`, `nanite_settings`, `collision_mode` [L]; for imported FBX use `StaticMeshEditorSubsystem.get_nanite_settings / set_nanite_settings`.
  4. One actor per chunk, `is_spatially_loaded=False` (roads are visible from mountain tops; about 1 M vertices in total, tens of MB) and `hlod_layer` empty.
  5. Surfaces: physical material comes from the road material or component override; the landscape keeps its own per-layer physical materials.
* GeometryScript can generate such strips directly if Blender is not wanted: `AddVerticesToMesh`, `AddTrianglesToMesh`, `SetMeshTriangleUVs`, `AppendSimpleSweptPolygon` (all in the stub), then `CopyMeshToStaticMesh` with `bApplyNaniteSettings` or `CreateNewStaticMeshAssetFromMesh`.

## 3. World Partition

### 3.1 Creating a WP map and what you get [L]

* Python: `unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.LevelEditorSubsystem).new_level("/Game/Forza/Maps/L_World", is_partitioned_world=True)` (stub signature `new_level(asset_path, is_partitioned_world=False)`), or `new_level_from_template(path, "/Engine/Maps/Templates/OpenWorld")`. Both save the map. C++: `GEditor->NewMap(true)` (what the subsystem calls) -> `UWorldFactory.bCreateWorldPartition`.
* New-map defaults come from `UWorldPartitionSettings`: `bNewMapsEnableWorldPartition=false` (the explicit `true` argument overrides), `bNewMapsEnableWorldPartitionStreaming=true`. `BaseEngine.ini [/Script/Engine.WorldPartitionSettings]` sets `RuntimeHashDefaultClass=WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet` and `EditorHashDefaultClass=WorldPartitionEditorSpatialHash`, default HLOD layer `/Engine/Maps/Templates/HLODs/HLODLayer_Instanced`.
* **5.8 uses `UWorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet`**, not the older SpatialHash grids. Config lives in `RuntimePartitions[]` (`FRuntimePartitionDesc{Name, MainLayer, HLODSetups[]}`) where `MainLayer` is a `URuntimePartitionLHGrid` (`CellSize`, `bIs2D`, `Origin`) with the shared `URuntimePartition` fields `LoadingRange`, `Priority`, `bBlockOnSlowStreaming`, `bClientOnlyVisible`, `BoundsMethod`. `SetDefaultValues()` creates partition "MainPartition": `LoadingRange=25600` (256 m), `CellSize=LoadingRange/2=12800` (128 m), `bIs2D=true`, plus one HLOD setup whose cell size/range double per level. The OpenWorld template map's binary contains the strings "MainGrid", `RuntimePartitionLHGrid`, `RuntimePartitionPersistent` and the HLOD layer `/Engine/OpenWorldTemplate/HLOD/HLOD0_Instancing`, so its partition is probably named "MainGrid" rather than "MainPartition" (do not hard-code the name; iterate the array as in 3.2).
* Python reach is limited [L stub]: `world.get_world_settings().world_partition` is read-only and returns `unreal.WorldPartition`, which only exposes `default_hlod_layer`, `runtime_cells_transformer_stack`, `has_standalone_hlod`, `server_streaming_*`. `RuntimeHash`, `RuntimePartitions`, `LoadingRange`, `CellSize` are **not** visible. Tune them in C++ (or hand-edit once in World Settings and keep the saved map as a template).

### 3.2 Numbers for high-speed driving [I unless noted]

* 250 km/h = 69 m/s. A 256 m range is 3.7 s of look-ahead: too short. Start at `LoadingRange = 76800` (768 m, the example Epic uses in the docs [W]) and `CellSize = 25600` (256 m). If cell loads hitch, shrink `CellSize` to 12800 but keep the range; each cell should hold at most a few hundred actors and ISMs of at most ~10k instances.
* Put an extra look-ahead streaming source on the car: `unreal.WorldPartitionStreamingSourceComponent` (`enable_streaming_source()` exists) positioned `speed * 2 s` ahead.
* Fewer partitions is better ("more than one grid can hurt performance" [W]); keep one main partition.
* CVars/commands [W/L]: `wp.Runtime.ToggleDrawRuntimeHash2D/3D`, `wp.Runtime.MaxLoadingLevelStreamingCells`, `wp.Runtime.HLOD 0`, `wp.Runtime.OverrideRuntimeSpatialHashLoadingRange` (SpatialHash only). 5.8 additions [W]: `s.ContinuouslyIncrementalGCWhileActorsPendingPurge`, WP Insights spatial profiler, World Settings "Dynamic Loading Range Scaling" (PIE startup).
* Reflection snippet to set the main partition (the properties are private, `URuntimePartition::LoadingRange` is public) [I - verify in editor after running]:
```cpp
#include "WorldPartition/WorldPartition.h"
#include "WorldPartition/RuntimeHashSet/WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet.h"
#include "WorldPartition/RuntimeHashSet/RuntimePartitionLHGrid.h"
UWorldPartition* WP = World->GetWorldPartition();
auto* Hash = WP ? Cast<UWorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet>(WP->RuntimeHash) : nullptr;
FArrayProperty* Arr = CastField<FArrayProperty>(UWorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet::StaticClass()->FindPropertyByName("RuntimePartitions"));
FScriptArrayHelper Helper(Arr, Arr->ContainerPtrToValuePtr<void>(Hash));
FStructProperty* Desc = CastFieldChecked<FStructProperty>(Arr->Inner);
for (int32 i = 0; i < Helper.Num(); ++i) {
  auto* MainProp = CastFieldChecked<FObjectProperty>(Desc->Struct->FindPropertyByName("MainLayer"));
  auto* Main = Cast<URuntimePartition>(MainProp->GetObjectPropertyValue_InContainer(Helper.GetRawPtr(i)));
  Main->LoadingRange = 76800;
  if (auto* Grid = Cast<URuntimePartitionLHGrid>(Main))
    *URuntimePartitionLHGrid::StaticClass()->FindPropertyByName("CellSize")->ContainerPtrToValuePtr<uint32>(Grid) = 25600;
}
// then re-save; HLOD partitions derive from the main one via UpdateHLODRuntimePartitionFrom() when edited through the details panel.
```

### 3.3 Landscape inside WP

* After Import the world is "grid based" and `ChangeGridSize(Info, N)` turns the single landscape into an `ALandscape` (non-streaming "parent") plus `ALandscapeStreamingProxy` actors of N x N components (editor default 2, UI range 1..16). `ALandscape::bAreNewLandscapeActorsSpatiallyLoaded` (Python `are_new_landscape_actors_spatially_loaded`, EditAnywhere) decides whether proxies and spline actors stream.
* For a 4 km world I recommend **proxies always loaded** (`False`): total landscape residency is a few hundred MB, mountains stay visible to the horizon, and you skip landscape HLOD (`ULandscapeHLODBuilder` exists if you ever stream it: `hlod_mesh_source_lod_policy`, `hlod_texture_size_policy` on the proxy; `ULandscapeSettings::HLODMaxTextureSize`).
* WP world gets landscape data in OFPA files: expect 1 file per proxy.

### 3.4 One File Per Actor (OFPA), actor counts, data layers

* Every actor is its own `.uasset`. **Never spawn one actor per tree/post.** Use instanced meshes (section 6). Spawning 100k actors from Python is also very slow.
* Actor fields (Python names): `is_spatially_loaded`, `runtime_grid`, `data_layer_assets`, `hlod_layer`, `enable_auto_lod_generation` ("Include Actor in HLOD"), `is_main_world_only`. A spatially loaded actor's bounds should stay below about one cell; huge bounds get promoted to higher grid levels or become effectively always loaded [I].
* `WorldSettings.instanced_foliage_grid_size` default **25600** (also `DefaultPlacementGridSize`, `LandscapeSplineMeshesGridSize`) controls how the foliage system partitions instances [L].
* Data layers: runtime states Unloaded / Loaded / Activated via `UDataLayerManager`; not needed for the base game. Possible later use: event props or race-only geometry. **SKIP for now.**
* Runtime cell transformers: `WorldPartition.runtime_cells_transformer_stack` + `UWorldPartitionRuntimeCellTransformerISM` (properties `AllowedClasses`, `DisallowedClasses`, `MinNumInstances`) can auto-merge many identical StaticMeshActors into ISMs at cook. An optional safety net, not a plan.

### 3.5 HLOD

* HLOD layer types [L stub]: `INSTANCING, MESH_MERGE, MESH_SIMPLIFY, MESH_APPROXIMATE, CUSTOM, CUSTOM_HLOD_ACTOR`. Layer fields: `CellSize`, `LoadingRange`, `bIsSpatiallyLoaded`, `ParentLayer`. Instancing swaps meshes for their lowest LOD instances (cheap, no baking, good with Nanite); Merged / Simplified build proxy meshes.
* Because landscape + roads are always loaded and streamed content is small, **HLOD is optional**. If you want distant trees or settlements: duplicate `/Engine/Maps/Templates/HLODs/HLODLayer_Instanced` into `/Game`, assign via `actor.set_editor_property("hlod_layer", layer)` or `world_partition.default_hlod_layer`. Foliage types have `include_in_hlod`.
* Build from the command line (flags verified in `WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder.cpp`: `SetupHLODs`, `BuildHLODs`, `RebuildHLODs`, `DeleteHLODs`, `FinalizeHLODs`, `DumpStats`, `ReportOnly`, `DistributedBuild`, `BuilderIdx=`, `BuildHLODLayer=`; with no explicit step flags it does setup + build):
```
"W:\Unreal Engine 5\UE_5.8\Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe" "<proj>\Sonnet55Forza.uproject" /Game/Forza/Maps/L_World ^
  -run=WorldPartitionBuilderCommandlet -Builder=WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder -AllowCommandletRendering ^
  -SetupHLODs -BuildHLODs -SCCProvider=None -Unattended -NoSplash -log
```
  The map must be the single bare token (commandlet errors with "Missing world name" otherwise) and **`-AllowCommandletRendering` is mandatory** for this builder (`RequiresCommandletRendering()`), the editor must not have the project open [W].
* Python (editor already open): `unreal.WorldPartitionHLODBlueprintLibrary.build_hlod_for_volume(box)` / `build_hlod_for_actors(actors)` (5.8; per-selection builds are one of its HLOD-UX features [W]).
* Other builders in the same family [W/L]: `WorldPartitionMiniMapBuilder` (editor preview texture only, `AWorldPartitionMiniMap` is editor-only - not suitable for the HUD; draw the HUD minimap from `roads.json` instead), `WorldPartitionFoliageBuilder -NewGridSize=<cm>` (re-grids foliage), `WorldPartitionNavigationDataBuilder`, `WorldPartitionResaveActorsBuilder -ActorClass=`, `WorldPartitionRenameDuplicateBuilder`, `PCGWorldPartitionBuilder -IncludeGraphNames=A;B`. All run as `-run=WorldPartitionBuilderCommandlet -Builder=<Class>`.
* Python entry from a shell: `UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe <uproject> -ExecutePythonScript="C:/path/script.py arg1" -unattended -nosplash` (quote handling documented in `EditorPythonExecuter.cpp`).

## 4. Nanite

Constraints that matter here [W unless noted]:

| Item | Rule for this project |
|---|---|
| Materials | Only **Opaque** and **Masked** are rendered by Nanite; anything else falls back to the default material with a log warning. No Mesh Decals (receiving projected decals is fine). Wireframe not supported. |
| Vertex interpolators / custom UVs | Work but evaluated 3x per pixel; avoid heavy per-pixel custom expressions (Parallax Occlusion Mapping may artifact). |
| Deformation | Rigid transforms and non-uniform scale fine. World Position Offset supported with limits; clamp displacement; set `WorldPositionOffsetDisableDistance` (component, Python `world_position_offset_disable_distance`; foliage type has the same + `evaluate_world_position_offset`). CVar `r.Nanite.Culling.WPODisableDistance` exists [L]. No morph targets. |
| Instance limit | 16 million streamed-in instances hard cap. |
| Components | Static, skeletal, ISM, spline mesh, HISM, geometry collection, foliage, landscape grass. |
| Tangents | Not stored per vertex; derived in the pixel shader (edge discontinuities possible). `bExplicitTangents` exists in `FMeshNaniteSettings`. |
| Unsupported | Forward shading, MSAA, VR stereo, lighting channels, min screen radius / distance culling. |
| Ray tracing | Uses the fallback mesh by default (lower `FallbackRelativeError` to keep more triangles). `r.RayTracing.Nanite.Mode 1` is experimental native Nanite RT. |
| Tessellation | Runtime Nanite tessellation / displacement exists; 5.8 adds `r.Shadow.Virtual.Nanite.AllowTessellationDirectional/Local`. **SKIP** for this game. |

`FMeshNaniteSettings` fields verified in `EngineTypes.h` and the stub (Python `unreal.MeshNaniteSettings`): `enabled, explicit_tangents, lerp_u_vs, separable, voxel_ndf, voxel_opacity, shape_preservation {NONE, PRESERVE_AREA, VOXELIZE}, position_precision, normal_precision, tangent_precision, bone_weight_precision, target_minimum_residency_in_kb, keep_percent_triangles, trim_relative_error, generate_fallback, fallback_target, fallback_percent_triangles, fallback_relative_error, max_edge_length_factor, num_rays, voxel_level, ray_back_up, displacement_uv_channel, displacement_maps, nanite_assembly_data`.
**Python pitfall:** the generated constructor defaults most numeric fields to 0, which differs from the C++ defaults (e.g. `position_precision` is "auto" = MIN_int32, `normal_precision` = -1, `fallback_relative_error` = 1.0). Always `s = sm_sub.get_nanite_settings(mesh)`, modify, `sm_sub.set_nanite_settings(mesh, s)` (`StaticMeshEditorSubsystem`), never build the struct from scratch.

### 4.1 Foliage, rocks, buildings

* **Foliage:** 5.7 introduced Nanite Foliage (voxels, assemblies, skinning), still labelled experimental in 5.8 [W]. The useful, stable part is `shape_preservation = VOXELIZE` (distant triangles become voxels so canopies keep their perceived volume) or `PRESERVE_AREA` (legacy). Voxel quality is controlled by `voxel_level`, `num_rays`, `voxel_ndf`, `voxel_opacity`. Treat as ADAPT: enable for trees/bushes, check visually, fall back to `PRESERVE_AREA`.
* **Masked leaves:** supported, but masked rasterization is programmable and costlier. `nanite_pixel_programmable_distance` (foliage type, ISM descriptor, static mesh scene proxy desc [L]) forcibly turns pixel-programmable raster off beyond a distance. Set it to a few tens of metres for leaf cards; far canopy is mostly voxels or opaque anyway.
* **Wind (WPO):** keep, but with `world_position_offset_disable_distance` (e.g. 3000 cm) because WPO invalidates cached VSM pages every frame (section 5.3).
* **Rocks, buildings, guard rails, signs:** straight Nanite, opaque; high poly is cheap. Skip lightmap UVs (`Generate Lightmap UVs` off; static lighting is off in this project, `r.AllowStaticLighting=False`).
* **Roads:** see 2.10.
* **Nanite assemblies:** new in 5.7 (API for creating them from Blueprint); experimental. SKIP.

## 5. Lumen, Virtual Shadow Maps, MegaLights

### 5.1 Lumen constraints for world content [W unless noted]

* Software ray tracing needs SM6 and **mesh distance fields** (project already has `r.GenerateMeshDistanceFields=True`). It traces each mesh's SDF for the first 2 m, then the merged Global Distance Field. Landscape is traced as a **heightfield** (`r.LumenScene.Heightfield.Tracing=1`, `...MaxTracingSteps=32` [L]).
* Distance-field GI supports static meshes, ISM, HISM and landscape; foliage must have "Affect Distance Field Lighting". **World Position Offset is not seen by software tracing.** The mesh's assigned material is used for the SDF, so overriding materials with different blend modes or two-sidedness causes mismatches.
* **Surface cache:** foliage and ISMs only get surface-cache coverage if they are **Nanite**. Static meshes get 12 cards by default (`Max Lumen Mesh Cards`, `MaxLumenMeshCards` build setting [L]). Spline meshes get refitted cards that degrade when heavily bent. Walls need >= 10 cm thickness.
* Materials that use Pixel Depth, Camera Position or Camera Vector need a Ray Tracing Quality Switch node to evaluate correctly in the surface cache.
* Software Lumen scene covers about 200 m from the camera by default (post process `Lumen Scene View Distance`, extendable to 800 m); hardware far field to 1 km needs `r.LumenScene.FarField=1`, HLOD1 and a matching `r.RayTracing.Culling.Radius`.
* `r.Lumen.TraceMeshSDFs.Allow` (0 = use Global SDF only): the engine text says per-mesh SDF tracing has high cost in scenes with high instance density (overlapping meshes). Scalability level High sets it to 0, Epic to 1 [L].
* **Hardware RT pitfall (this project):** `r.Lumen.HardwareRayTracing` defaults to **1** [L] and the project has `r.RayTracing=True`, so an RTX 5070 will use HW Lumen. Epic documents significant scene-update cost for hardware RT in scenes above about 100,000 instances, and Fortnite Chapter 4 had to switch to software tracing to reach 60 fps. A foliage-heavy driving game is that case. **Recommendation:** `r.Lumen.HardwareRayTracing=0` and, unless something else needs it, `r.RayTracing=False` in DefaultEngine.ini (smaller shader set, no BVH). Re-test with HW RT only if reflections look wrong.

### 5.2 Recommended settings for 60 fps on an RTX 5070-class GPU [I, grounded in local scalability data]

Verified building blocks (`Engine\Config\BaseScalability.ini`, 5.8):
* `sg.GlobalIlluminationQuality`: 0 Lumen off; **1 = Lumen Lite (Beta, new in 5.8, "about twice as fast as High", Irradiance Fields with probe occlusion; reflections fall back to SSR at `sg.ReflectionQuality=1`)** [W]; **2 = High** (ScreenProbeGather, `r.Lumen.TraceMeshSDFs.Allow=0`, `r.LumenScene.SurfaceCache.AtlasSize=3584`, `r.Lumen.ScreenProbeGather.TracingOctahedronResolution=8`, translucency volume `GridPixelSize=64`); 3 = Epic (turns mesh SDF tracing and HW hit-lighting on).
* `sg.ReflectionQuality=2`: Lumen reflections, `r.Lumen.Reflections.DownsampleFactor=2`.
* `sg.ShadowQuality=2`: `r.Shadow.Virtual.MaxPhysicalPages=2048`, SMRT 8 rays/4 samples directional, 4/4 local; 3 = 4096 pages.
* Epic's Lumen page says the High level targets 60 fps for large open worlds on current consoles; a 5070 is well above that class.

Suggested starting point:
```
; DefaultEngine.ini [/Script/Engine.RendererSettings] (project settings)
r.DynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod=1
r.ReflectionMethod=1
r.Shadow.Virtual.Enable=1
r.GenerateMeshDistanceFields=True
r.RayTracing=False                      ; was True. Recommended off if not used elsewhere
; [SystemSettings] / DefaultScalability
sg.GlobalIlluminationQuality=2          ; fall back to 1 (Lumen Lite) if GPU bound
sg.ReflectionQuality=2
sg.ShadowQuality=2
r.Lumen.HardwareRayTracing=0
r.Lumen.TraceMeshSDFs.Allow=0
r.LumenScene.Heightfield.Tracing=1
r.AntiAliasingMethod=4                  ; TSR
r.ScreenPercentage=70                   ; TSR upscaling (67-77 is the usual band)
```
Post-process volume: leave `Lumen Scene View Distance` at default or 300-400 m; raise `Lumen Scene Lighting Update Speed` / `Final Gather Lighting Update Speed` (Advanced) so GI follows a moving sun, at some cost; keep `Max Trace Distance` large enough for valleys and tunnel mouths (too small leaks light).

### 5.3 Virtual Shadow Maps (VSM)

* Facts [W]: 16k x 16k virtual maps, 128 x 128 pages, cached between frames. Nanite always renders into VSM; non-Nanite geometry is "much more expensive", Epic recommends Nanite for every supported mesh. Moving or rotating a light invalidates all of its cached pages. WPO / PDO invalidate the touched pages every frame. Directional clipmap levels default 6..22 (level 6 ~ 64 cm, doubling per level; 22 ~ 40 km), `r.Shadow.Virtual.Clipmap.FirstLevel/LastLevel` adjust it. Exceeding `r.Shadow.Virtual.MaxPhysicalPages` corrupts shadows. `r.Shadow.Virtual.UseFarShadowCulling 0` makes non-Nanite behave like Nanite. Many large local lights are costly.
* Consequences for time-of-day: **do not rotate the sun every frame.** Quantize the DirectionalLight rotation (for example every 0.5-1.0 s, a step of a fraction of a degree) so cached pages survive between updates, and expect one expensive frame per step. Keep the ordinary 24 min-per-day scale so steps are tiny.
* Non-Nanite landscape has extra VSM invalidation controls (`non_nanite_virtual_shadow_map_*` on the landscape actor [L stub]); with Nanite landscape these are moot, one more reason to use Nanite landscape.
* Reasonable trims for a 4 km world [I]: `r.Shadow.Virtual.Clipmap.LastLevel` around 19 (about 5 km radius) instead of 22; keep `ResolutionLodBiasDirectional` at 0 unless close-up shadows are soft.
* 5.8 adds an experimental "prefiltered distant" shadow path (`r.Shadow.Virtual.PrefilteredDistant.ProjectEnable`) and `r.Shadow.Virtual.DeferredInvalidationBudget` to throttle `r.Nanite.VSMInvalidateOnLODDelta` [W, secondary]. Not needed at first.

### 5.4 MegaLights

Production-ready in 5.8 (transmission, froxel translucency, IES for volumetrics, cloud shadows; goal 60 fps) [W]. Potentially attractive for night driving with many street lights and headlights. It is not required for the baseline: **SKIP initially**, re-evaluate when the night look is built. `r.MegaLights.Supported 0` removes its shader cost if unused [W, secondary].

## 6. Scatter: PCG vs our own instanced meshes

### 6.1 PCG facts [L/W]

* Plugin `PCG` is on by default in 5.8 and already enabled in the .uproject. Generation modes: non-partitioned, partitioned (`APCGPartitionActor`, grid chosen by `PCGWorldActor` "Partition Grid Size" or by Grid Size nodes), hierarchical (HiGen) and runtime (`EPCGComponentGenerationTrigger::GenerateOnLoad / GenerateOnDemand / GenerateAtRuntime`, scheduled around PCG generation sources). Commandlet builder `PCGWorldPartitionBuilder` (`pcg.BuildComponents` console equivalent). 5.8 improvements [W]: GPU runtime scatter on par with landscape grass, actor/component-less runtime generation, scheduler game-thread cost down to ~30 %.
* Python can author graphs: `unreal.PCGGraph.add_node_of_type(settings_class)`, `add_edge(from, pin, to, pin)`; component `generate(force)`, `cleanup(remove_components)`; node settings classes in the stub: `PCGSurfaceSamplerSettings`, `PCGStaticMeshSpawnerSettings`, `PCGSplineSamplerSettings`, `PCGGetLandscapeSettings`, `PCGMeshSelectorWeighted`, `PCGSoftISMComponentDescriptor`.
* Caveats: generation is asynchronous (scripts must poll or use the builder commandlet); partitioned output creates many partition actors/files; needs the landscape cache for runtime generation (forum report: "Always Serialize") [W, secondary]; output reproducibility depends on component seed + graph + partition grid.

### 6.2 Recommendation

Use our own deterministic scatter: the generator already writes `placements/*.json|bin` per cell (WORLD_SPEC section 5). Two implementations, pick one:

| | Foliage API from Python | Own `ARoamScatterCell` actor |
|---|---|---|
| Call | `unreal.InstancedFoliageActor.add_instances(world, foliage_type, transforms)` [L: `AInstancedFoliageActor::AddInstances`, editor-only static UFUNCTION; routes every transform to the right partitioned foliage actor through `AInstancedFoliageActor::Get(World, true, PersistentLevel, Location)`] | `UFUNCTION AddInstances(UStaticMesh*, TArray<FTransform>)` creating one `UInstancedStaticMeshComponent` per mesh |
| WP partitioning | automatic, grid = `WorldSettings.instanced_foliage_grid_size` (25600) | you choose cell size = streaming cell |
| C++ needed | none | runtime-module actor + editor wrapper |
| Re-runs | `remove_all_instances(world, foliage_type)` | destroy actors by folder/tag |
| Per-instance custom data | no | yes (`NumCustomDataFloats`) |
| Component class | `FoliageType_InstancedStaticMesh.component_class` (must derive from `FoliageInstancedStaticMeshComponent`, which is HISM based) | plain ISM |
| Settings | `FoliageType_InstancedStaticMesh`: `mesh`, `cull_distance`, `cast_shadow`, `affect_distance_field_lighting`, `evaluate_world_position_offset`, `world_position_offset_disable_distance`, `nanite_pixel_programmable_distance`, `nanite_override_materials`, `body_instance`, `include_in_hlod`, `mobility`, `receives_decals` | on the component |

I would start with the Foliage API for trees, bushes, rocks (zero C++), and use the cell actor only where custom data or exotic layouts are required. HISM vs ISM [I]: for Nanite meshes plain ISM is enough (Nanite culls per instance on the GPU); HISM builds a CPU cluster tree (`BuildTreeIfOutdated`) and is worth it only for non-Nanite meshes with distance LODs. Check the cost of the HISM-based foliage component in the profiler; if it matters, use the cell actor.

Generic ISM API verified [L stub]: `add_instances(transforms, should_return_indices, world_space=False, update_navigation=True)`, `set_cull_distances`, `set_num_custom_data_floats`. Components created in the editor must be registered with `AddInstanceComponent()` to be saved with the actor.

Determinism rules: seed every generator with a hash of `(world_seed, cell_x, cell_y, species)`, sort inputs before use, write transforms in a fixed order, and never read `FMath::Rand`.

## 7. Water plugin

* [L] `Plugins\Experimental\Water\Water.uplugin`: `IsExperimentalVersion: true`, `EnabledByDefault: false`, hard dependencies Landmass (Beta), Niagara, GeometryProcessing, BlueprintMaterialTextureNodes. Already enabled in the project. Content under `/Water/...`.
* Classes in the Python stub: `WaterBody` (abstract), `WaterBodyOcean`, `WaterBodyLake`, `WaterBodyRiver`, `WaterBodyCustom`, `WaterBodyIsland`, `WaterBodyExclusionVolume`, `WaterZone`, and components `WaterBodyOceanComponent` etc., `WaterSplineComponent` (a `SplineComponent`).
* Spawning from Python: `eas.spawn_actor_from_class(unreal.WaterBodyOcean, loc)` / `unreal.WaterZone`. **Pitfall [L]:** the editor *factory* (`WaterBodyActorFactory.cpp`) applies defaults after spawn: `WaterMaterial`, `WaterStaticMeshMaterial`, `HLODMaterial`, `UnderwaterPostProcessMaterial`, water-info material, default spline points, and (ocean) default `WaterWaves`, `FillWaterZoneWithOcean()`. A plain `spawn_actor_from_class` skips all of it. Set them yourself:
  * default material paths found in `WaterEditorSettings.cpp`: `/Water/Materials/WaterSurface/Water_Material_Ocean`, `..._Lake`, `..._River`, `Water_FarMesh`, `/Water/Materials/PostProcessing/M_UnderWater_PostProcess_Volume`, `/Water/Materials/HLOD/HLODWater`, mesh `/Water/Meshes/S_WaterPlane_256`.
  * properties (stub): `water_body.get_water_body_component().set_editor_property("water_material", mat)`, `affects_landscape`, `shape_dilation`, `water_mesh_override`; zone: `zone_extent` (Vector2D, cm), `render_target_resolution` (IntPoint), `auto_include_landscapes_as_terrain`.
  * Spline: `ResetSpline` is not scriptable, but `WaterSplineComponent` inherits `SplineComponent` (`add_spline_point`, `clear_spline_points`, `set_closed_loop`). Per-point depth/width/velocity live in `WaterSplineMetadata`.
  * `UWaterBodyOceanComponent::FillWaterZoneWithOcean()` is `CallInEditor` (callable from Python).
* Landscape carving requires **Edit Layers + the Water brush / Landmass** [W] (alpha-blend, min, max, additive carve modes; lakes and oceans need all points at one height). Reliable scripted alternative: carve basins and the sea bed into the heightmap yourself, set `affects_landscape=False`.
* Decisions: **Ocean ADAPT** (one body + one zone sized to cover the east coast; sea level 0), **Lake ADAPT** (only if a lake exists), **River SKIP** (needs per-point metadata and carving; WORLD_SPEC's river "Silverrun" can be a flat-shaded ribbon mesh with a water material), **carving SKIP**. A cheaper fallback if the plugin causes trouble: a large plane with a Single Layer Water material at Z=0.
* Water mesh is quad-tree tessellated from a water-info render target per zone; keep zone extent as small as the visible coast needs, as the info texture resolution is shared across the zone [I].

## 8. Sky, atmosphere, clouds, fog, lights: dynamic time of day and weather

Components and verified Python property names (stub):

| Component | Properties to drive |
|---|---|
| `SkyAtmosphere` (`SkyAtmosphereComponent`) | `transform_mode` (`PLANET_TOP_AT_ABSOLUTE_WORLD_ORIGIN` = ground at Z=0), `bottom_radius`, `atmosphere_height`, `multi_scattering_factor` (keep 1), `trace_sample_count_scale`, `height_fog_contribution` |
| `DirectionalLightComponent` x2 | `atmosphere_sun_light=True`, `atmosphere_sun_light_index` (0 sun, 1 moon), `per_pixel_atmosphere_transmittance`, `cast_cloud_shadows`, `cloud_shadow_strength`, `cast_shadows_on_clouds`, `cast_shadows_on_atmosphere`, `cloud_scattered_luminance_scale`, `light_source_angle` |
| `VolumetricCloud` | `material`, `layer_bottom_altitude`, `layer_height`, `tracing_start_max_distance`, `tracing_max_distance`, `view_sample_count_scale` |
| `ExponentialHeightFog` | `fog_density`, `fog_height_falloff`, `fog_max_opacity`, `start_distance`, `sky_atmosphere_ambient_contribution_color_scale`, volumetric fog |
| `SkyLightComponent` | `real_time_capture=True`, `lower_hemisphere_is_black` |

Best practice (Epic's Sky Atmosphere and Volumetric Cloud pages plus local data):
* Setup order: SkyAtmosphere, Directional light(s) with *Atmosphere Sun Light* ticked, SkyLight with **Real Time Capture** (its cost is spread over 9 frames), VolumetricCloud with a volume material, ExponentialHeightFog. Enable project setting "Support Sky Atmosphere Affecting Height Fog" and set the fog inscattering colours to black so the atmosphere colours the fog [W]. The engine template `/Engine/Maps/Templates/TimeOfDay_Default` shows a working arrangement (DirectionalLight + SkyLight + SkyAtmosphere + VolumetricCloud + `SM_SkySphere` with `M_AdvancedSkyDome`) [L, from the .umap strings].
* Calibration [W]: sun about 120,000 lux at zenith, angular diameter 0.545 degrees; moon about 0.26 lux, 0.568 degrees. This project already sets `r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure.ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange=True`, which is what physical values need. Keep multiscattering 1; the second directional light gets less sky impact because multiple scattering is only evaluated for the first.
* **Sea level at Z = 0** and the atmosphere transform mode above means aerial perspective and the ocean line up. In the heightmap encoding (2.3) map sea level to world Z=0.
* Sun path (simple, good enough): `SunPitch = -90 * sin(2*pi*(hour-6)/24)` degrees (0 at 06:00 and 18:00, -90 at noon), yaw = fixed azimuth plus `15*(hour-12)` degrees; moon = opposite direction. Fade lights through the atmosphere automatically (transmittance does the reddening), do not hand-colour the sun.
* Update the sun rotation in quantized steps (see 5.3). Real-time sky capture handles the ambient change; avoid `RecaptureSky` calls.
* Cloud material: engine default `/Engine/EngineSky/VolumetricClouds/m_SimpleVolumetricCloud_Inst` exposes scalar parameters such as `Cloud_GlobalCoverage`, `Cloud_GlobalDensity`, `Cloud_AlbedoColor`, `Storm_AlbedoColor`, `Storm_LightningClouds`, `WindMultiplier`, plus textures `T_CloudMask`, `T_CloudPattern` [L, parameter names read from the .uasset]. Drive weather by making a dynamic material instance of it (or an MPC) and lerping coverage/density/colours.
* Performance [L/W]: `r.VolumetricRenderTarget.Mode` default 0 (quarter-res trace, reconstruct, upsample) is the right mode for a fast-moving camera; 1 = half-res; 2 = quarter-res full-res reconstruct but cannot intersect opaque meshes. Volumetric clouds are not supported on mobile; `r.VolumetricCloud.*` sample caps exist. SkyAtmosphere LUT sizes: `r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT.Width/Height` (256 suggested for cloud shadows), `r.SkyAtmosphere.AerialPerspectiveLUT.Width/DepthResolution` (3D texture, memory heavy).
* Weather: expose one `MPC_Weather` (Wetness, RainIntensity, Snow) read by road/landscape materials; rain as a camera-attached Niagara system; fog density/height falloff curves; cloud parameters; `directional light cloud_shadow_strength`; wet surfaces lower roughness. Lumen needs no special handling. A Single Layer Water material for puddles/sea.
* Not needed: the `SunPosition` plugin (latitude/longitude/date driven sun; off by default), a Weather plugin (none ships with 5.8). Engine content has `T_Sky_Stars` and `SM_SkySphere` for a night star dome [L].

## 9. Concrete end-to-end pipeline (script-driven, re-runnable)

| # | Step | Where | API / command |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Generate heightmap (r16), weightmaps (r8, normalised), `world_meta.json` with `ZScale`, `ActorZ`, `ScaleXY`, vertex count | `Tools/world/build_world.py` (numpy) | Mapping from 2.3; road corridors carved here |
| 2 | Add `Sonnet55ForzaEditor` module with `RoamWorldBuilder` (CreateLandscapeFromHeightmap, BuildLandscapeAll, ConfigureWorldPartition, optional SetHeightmap) | C++ | 2.4, 3.2; build with `Build.bat Sonnet55ForzaEditor Win64 Development -Project=...` while the editor is closed |
| 3 | Create the WP map | Python | `LevelEditorSubsystem.new_level(path, True)` |
| 4 | Tune runtime partition (768 m range, 256 m cell), set `bEnableStreaming` true | C++ call from Python | 3.2 |
| 5 | Create layer infos, physical materials, landscape material (and MPC) | Python + C++ helper | 2.5, 2.6; `MaterialEditingLibrary` |
| 6 | Create landscape from r16 + weightmaps, `ChangeGridSize(Info, 4)`, proxies always loaded | C++ via Python | 2.4 |
| 7 | `enable_nanite=True`, `BuildLandscapeAll()` (Nanite + grass maps + physical material), wait for async Nanite builds | Python + C++ | 2.7; confirm in log |
| 8 | Import Blender road/bridge/tunnel chunks (FBX) as Nanite meshes, spawn one actor per chunk, `is_spatially_loaded=False` | Python | 2.10 |
| 9 | Scatter: foliage types (Nanite, voxelize, WPO disable distance) then `InstancedFoliageActor.add_instances` per species in batches (e.g. 50k transforms) | Python | 6.2 |
| 10 | Lighting actors: SkyAtmosphere, 2 directional lights, SkyLight (real-time capture), VolumetricCloud, ExponentialHeightFog, ocean `WaterZone` + `WaterBodyOcean` | Python | 7, 8 |
| 11 | Optional HLODs | commandlet | 3.5 |
| 12 | Save everything: `unreal.EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.save_dirty_packages(True, True)`; verify `stat unit`, `wp.Runtime.ToggleDrawRuntimeHash2D`, Nanite visualization, `landscape.DumpTargetLayerAllocations` [L] | Python / console | |

Run non-interactively: `UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe <uproject> -ExecutePythonScript="Tools/ue/step.py" -unattended -nosplash -log` (editor commandlet rendering may be required for Nanite builds; if a step needs the GPU use `UnrealEditor.exe` with `-ExecutePythonScript` instead of `-Cmd`) [I].

## 10. Pitfalls checklist

1. `ALandscape::Import` is C++ only; Python cannot create a landscape, and `LandscapeLayerInfoObject.layer_name` is read-only in Python (5.8).
2. Set landscape actor **scale before** `Import` (normals use it); keys of the height/layer TMaps must be `FGuid()`; component divisibility is silent on failure; layer data must be full size or empty; layers with data need a non-null `LayerInfo`.
3. All landscapes use edit layers in 5.7+; `Import` creates the default layer. Direct writes (`SetHeightmapData`) go to the current layer.
4. WP: more than 16 components per axis triggers the "landscape regions" flow in the editor UI path (needs a saved map, makes LocationVolumes). Stay <= 16/axis or save the map first.
5. WP defaults are 256 m range / 128 m cells (`RuntimeHashSet`). Too short for 250 km/h. Python cannot edit it.
6. Python cannot add arbitrary components to actors (`add_component_by_class` is not in the stub): use the Foliage API, a C++ cell actor, or a Blueprint actor that already owns an ISM.
7. Nanite landscape builds are async; unsaved or stale Nanite data = non-Nanite fallback in editor and a slow rebuild at cook. Keep `landscape.Nanite.UpdateLag` in mind when scripting edits.
8. `MeshNaniteSettings()` in Python zero-initialises numeric fields; always get/modify/set.
9. HW Lumen is on by default and the project enables ray tracing; many instances make it expensive. Turn it off for the 60 fps target.
10. Non-Nanite foliage is invisible to the Lumen surface cache and costly in VSM; WPO is invisible to software Lumen; WPO invalidates VSM pages each frame.
11. Rotating the sun each frame defeats VSM page caching.
12. Thin road ribbons leak light in Lumen software tracing: add thickness; spline meshes + Nanite have open bugs.
13. OFPA: one file per actor; never one actor per instance. Foliage grid default 256 m.
14. Plain `spawn_actor_from_class` for Water bodies skips the factory defaults (materials, waves, zone fill).
15. Water landscape carving needs Edit Layers + Landmass brushes; prefer pre-carving.
16. Live Coding cannot add the new editor module; do a full UBT build with the editor closed. The `.uproject` and Target files need edits.
17. No numpy in UE's Python: keep heavy math outside or in C++.
18. WORLD_SPEC says "127 quads" for a component made of two 63-quad sections (really 126).
19. Commandlets: HLOD builder needs `-AllowCommandletRendering`, the map as bare token, and no open editor instance.
20. Epic's docs page for the commandlet reference omits the `-SetupHLODs/-BuildHLODs/-DeleteHLODs` flags; they are real (source: `WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder.cpp`; the HLOD docs page lists them).

Keep `heightmap_4033.r16` naming only if you stay on option C; the r16/weightmap loader in 2.4 works for any size. Update `ZScale`: span 820 m -> `ZScale = 82000/512 = 160.16`.
